verified.bloom_gates: G1: yes, named counterparty (FDA). G2: yes, concrete dated commitment (PDUFA 2026-12-22, NDA accepted 2026-03). G3: weak. AstraZeneca's Baxfendy (baxdrostat), the first approved drug in this class, was cleared on 2026-05-18, so lorundrostat's approval risk is largely de-risked and visible. What stays unpriced is commercial share as the second drug to market, not the approval itself.
verified.edge: M. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: about -13%. The stock was $26.97 on 2026-04-04, after the NDA acceptance made the date public, and is $23.37 now (-51% from the $47.65 high in Nov-2025), so the PDUFA has not been bid into. Remaining upside: about +25-35% to roughly $30-32 on approval (still a low EV against a $1B+ US launch, with the royalty now bought out). Downside on a CRL: about -45-55% to roughly $11-13 (net cash about $6.4/share). Probability-weighted (about 85-90% approval given the class precedent): roughly $28.5-29, or about +22%. Edge is moderate, not high. Approval is the consensus expectation after Baxfendy, and the derating mostly reflects being second to market behind AstraZeneca, which approval alone does not fix.

verified.analysis: Verified: the PDUFA is 2026-12-22, unfired and still on track as of the Q2 release (2026-08-11). The stock is near its 52-week low ($21.46-47.65) and below its 50- and 200-day averages, so there has been no pre-event run-up. The capital structure supports the equity on its own: about $661M of cash on 2026-06-30 against $100M drawn on a $500M facility (later tranches need approval and sales milestones), plus the $200M Tanabe royalty buyout, gives net cash of about $560M and an EV of about $1.5B. The hold-back from ACTIVE is that the class precedent (AZ Baxfendy, approved 2026-05-18, similar add-on label) makes approval close to expected. Upside then depends on lorundrostat's label and pricing versus AstraZeneca's distribution reach, and a CRL would hit hard. Gaps: Q2 cash came from secondary summaries rather than the 10-Q, and there was no options-implied move check.

verified.bloom_gates: G1 YES: named counterparties, namely Oasis with four named nominees plus Chapek's paid advisory deal, and Matthew Prince's standing Park City offer. G2 NO: no concrete commitment. Oasis has not started soliciting votes, Vail's CEO says no sale is planned and Park City is 'not for sale', and the meeting date is unset. G3 NO: no specific unpriced figure. Prince's offer has no disclosed price (only a $500M pledge to invest in the resort), and Oasis cites a peer-relative discount without a number.
verified.edge: M-/L. Run-up: +12.4% from the pre-catalyst base of $129.93 (2026-06-17 close, the day before the Semafor proxy-fight report sent the stock +11%) to $146.03. The 2026-09-09 base before the 13D was $130.33, giving the same +12%. Remaining: about +20% to +36% only if there is a full sale. That range comes from my own capital-structure work, not an analyst target: FY27 Resort EBITDA guide midpoint $835M, about $2.92B net debt ($3.19B debt minus about $0.27B cash and CDs at 7/31/26), no preferred ahead of the common, about 35.6M shares. At 11x the equity is worth about $176/share, at 12x about $199, versus about 9.7x EV/EBITDA today. Probability-weighted (about 25% sale or review, about 45% board-seat settlement, about 30% Vail wins) the value is about $152, roughly +4%. That means about half the realistic proxy-fight premium is already harvested, and the larger upside depends on an outcome management is openly refusing.
verified.primary_source: SEC Schedule 13D (Oasis, filed 2026-09-16, notice dated 2026-09-10) and 13D/A dated 2026-09-29 (sec.gov 0000902664-26-003832 / -003970); Vail DEFA14A September 2026 (sec.gov 0000812011-26-000039); Vail FY2026 8-K results released 2026-09-28 (debt $3.19B, 3.9x leverage, FY27 EBITDA guide $805-865M); KPCW 2026-09-16; FMP EOD prices 2026-06-17 to 2026-10-09.
verified.analysis: The activist event is real and specific: 13D, four named nominees, paid nominee agreements, and a December meeting in practice. But the catalyst the market cares about (a sale or a Park City disposal) has no price, no commitment and no date, and the board-seat vote is not a value-realization event in itself. The equity waterfall is clean (no preferred, 3.9x leverage), so the sale case does mechanically support $176-199. The stock has already re-rated about 12% from the $130 base, and a likely settlement outcome leaves little residual, so this is a WATCH, not ACTIVE. Upgrade if Oasis files a definitive proxy with a dated meeting, if Vail opens a strategic review, or if a priced bid for Park City or the whole company appears. Gaps: the 10-10/10-12 tape was not checked, the pass-unit -10% figure was not re-verified, and lease liabilities and noncontrolling interests are not netted (they would modestly lower the sale-case value per share).

verified.analysis: The IPO plan is real and reported twice (Reuters via Kitco/MiningWeekly 2026-03-18/19; Aug-2026 ReporteMinero/MiningReporters), but it is only a target. It depends on market conditions, there is no filing, and McEwen Copper IPO timelines have slipped before (2022, 2023). Equity waterfall: the $457M implied stake is ~43% of MUX's market cap. The rest covers the San Jose 49% interest (dividends of $58.2M YTD) and the Timmins/Fox and Gold Bar mines, with $130M of debt principal ahead of the common and no preferred stock. The main issue is that the $4B financing needs ~$600M of equity from existing holders, which MUX cannot fund pro rata from $79M of cash. So the event could crystallize value and dilute MUX at the same time. Score is capped at 4 because the event is undated and uncommitted and the dilution-adjusted upside is modest and uncertain. Gap: I did not open the 10-Q directly; the Q2 figures come from Quartr and GlobeNewswire summaries, and the last-round per-share price was not checked.
